title: Short Stuff: Captain Santa
summary: Christmas Day Short Stuff episode on Captain Santa (Herman Schuenemann), a Chicago Christmas tree schooner captain whose ship, the Rouse Simmons, was lost in a November 1912 Lake Michigan storm. Covers the tradition of selling trees from schooners at the Clark Street docks, Schuenemann's background and debts, the final voyage, the search and discovery of the wreck and wallet, the family's continuing tree business, and the Coast Guard Mackinaw's annual tree delivery in his honor.
topics: US Coast Guard Cutter Mackinaw Christmas trees

segments.title: Christmas Day greetings and maritime disaster warning
segments.summary: The hosts welcome listeners on Christmas Day and note the episode is another maritime disaster story, though a festive one.

segments.title: Chicago's Christmas tree ships
segments.summary: In late 19th-century Chicago, captains sailed schooners loaded with trees from northern Michigan and Wisconsin to the Clark Street docks, where people could pick out trees; Captain Santa gave trees free to those down on their luck. German Christmas tree tradition spread via Prince Albert.

segments.title: Herman Schuenemann and the nickname Captain Santa
segments.summary: Herman Schuenemann, a German-born captain, owned a one-eighth share of the Rouse Simmons and was in debt from a failed saloon. He was known for generosity, and Chicago papers gave him the name Captain Santa. Brother August also sold trees along Lake Michigan.

segments.title: Final voyage and disappearance in November 1912
segments.summary: The Rouse Simmons set sail November 22, 1912, loaded with three to five thousand trees. Its flag at half-mast was spotted near Kewaunee; the motorboat from Two Rivers went out too late and could not find the ship in the snowstorm. Earlier, August had died in a 1898 tree-ship loss.

segments.title: Family worry, wreckage, and Captain Santa's wallet
segments.summary: Barbara and her daughters waited for the ship to arrive before worrying. Christmas trees washed up on Wisconsin shores and the ship was never seen again; up to 23 people died, possibly including lumberjacks. In 1924 Captain Santa's wallet was found in a fishing net. Barbara continued the tree business, later moving to trains and a lot; the loss marked the end of the schooner tree trade.

segments.title: Wreck discovery and legends of preserved trees
segments.summary: Rumors say evergreen scent lingers and trees may be preserved on the lake bottom. In 1971 a diver found the wreck at about 172 feet; a 2006 underwater archaeology survey documented it upright with tree timbers around it. The evergreen scent is said to be near Barbara's grave at Acacia Park Cemetery.

segments.title: Legend of the girl at the docks and annual Coast Guard tribute
segments.summary: A legend says a poor girl waited at the Clark Street docks for Captain Santa and was left waiting. Each December, the Coast Guard Cutter Mackinaw retraces the voyage and brings Christmas trees to Chicago's disadvantaged kids. Sources cited include Glen V. Longacre's 2006 Prologue article and Atlas Obscura.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wish listeners Merry Christmas and close the episode, followed by the network credit.
